montstmichelabbey.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
montstmichelabbey.slogan: An abbey crowned by an archangel, ringed by 14 metres of tide.
montstmichelabbey.line: Legend says the archangel Michael appeared in 708 to Aubert, bishop of Avranches, and told him to build a church on this rock.

arromanchesdebarquement.name: Arromanches Mulberry Harbour
arromanchesdebarquement.slogan: The harbour the Allies built themselves and towed across the Channel.
arromanchesdebarquement.line: About 116 concrete Phoenix caissons were sunk off Arromanches in June 1944, and the remains are still visible from the beach.

abbayeauxhommes.name: Abbaye aux Hommes
abbayeauxhommes.slogan: Nine spires over the tomb of the Conqueror.
abbayeauxhommes.line: William the Conqueror founded the abbey in 1063, and only one thigh bone of his remains still lies in the tomb.

pegasusbridgebenouville.name: Pegasus Bridge
pegasusbridgebenouville.slogan: Gliders in the night, a canal bridge, and the first minutes of D-Day.
pegasusbridgebenouville.line: Gliders landed as close as 43 metres to their objectives; the original bridge now stands at the Pegasus Museum.

memorialcaen.name: Mémorial de Caen
memorialcaen.slogan: A museum for peace, built on a wartime bunker.
memorialcaen.line: Opened by President Mitterrand on 6 June 1988, it now holds a fragment of the Berlin Wall and a Nobel Peace Prize gallery.
